surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Quinn sparks the Sabres back from two down
paras: Ryan Donato and Tyler Bertuzzi scored three and a half minutes apart early in the first to put the Blackhawks up 2-0. Jack Quinn got the Sabres on the board five minutes later, and Tage Thompson made it 2-2 early in the second. Oliver Moore gave the Hawks the lead late in the period, but they didn’t score again. Rasmus Dahlin tied it 3-3 for Buffalo early in the third, and Jiří Kulich put the Sabres ahead for good with less than seven minutes left.

The Sabres carried the play, outshooting the Blackhawks 28-15, and got the result to match. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 12 saves for the Sabres, and Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 28. By our Swing measure, Alex Vlasic had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Sabres moved to 1-1-0, climbing out of last place in the NHL. The Blackhawks dropped to 0-3-0, still last in the NHL.

items.text: Louis Crevier played his first game against Chicago since leaving, and picked up an assist.
The Blackhawks are on a three-game losing streak.
The Sabres won their home opener and have beaten the Blackhawks seven straight times, going back to the 2023-24 season.
